newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK, Canada sign pacts to fight illegal immigration.
newsitem.headline: HK, Canada sign pacts to fight illegal immigration.

text.p: Hong Kong and Canada said on Friday they had signed agreements aimed at combating illegal immigration.
Under the pacts, there will be an increase in cooperation in investigating and prosecuting immigrant smugglers and dealers in fraudulent documents, the two governments said in separate statements.
They will also guard against and investigate any abuse of their respective passports and other immigration documents, and will exchange information on illegal migration and smuggling.
The accords also codified existing practices that each side will accept the return of its people deemed inadmissible to the other's territory.
Canada is one of the most popular destinations for Asians seeking a better life overseas.
The country's police recently broke up a ring that smuggled Asians into North America where they were ultimately enslaved in prostitution, gambling and sweatshops.
Criminal gangs, or triads, that smuggle Chinese immigrants through the British colony of Hong Kong have raised concerns in Canada.
The British National (Overseas) travel documents issued to Hong Kong residents are often forged for human trafficking.
Some Western diplomats fear this trend will grow after the colony's reverts to China next July 1 to becomes a Chinese Special Administrative Region (SAR).

The Canadian government said the signing of the accords was "an important milestone before we render a decision about whether to offer visa-free access to Canada for qualified residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region".
Canada had said it agreed in principle to grant visa-free entry to SAR passport holders.
